mutation: PROMPT.md §5.2, extension #2: ATR-based minimum-risk filter (skip trades whose stop distance is narrower than the ATR multiple)
why_this_mutation: It is the only optional mutation that moved the cost drag materially: the cost-drag leg (results/20261021_102500_cost_drag_leg) measured, on 200 re-run cells, a mean net PF of 0.2281 on the parent and 0.5460 on the child, on 17 929 trades instead of 75 005. The mechanism is documented there: the cost of a trade as a share of its gross P&L is 2 * cost_per_side / risk_pct, and the median cell's stop distance is 0.912 % of the entry price, so a wider stop buys back the cost drag.

parent.description: The baseline grid: 266 symbols x 66 EMA pairs = 17 556 cells, full sample, min_risk_atr false.

child.description: The same grid with the ATR minimum-risk filter switched on. Everything else is held fixed: same symbols, same 66 pairs, same costs, same fill rule, same same-bar conflict rule, same sizing.
child.invocation: PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/run_grid.py --n 266 --min-risk-atr --atr-threshold 1.0 --engine fast --note 'pre-registered PROMPT.md 5.2 ATR minimum-risk mutation (preregistration_id atr_min_risk_1.0_full_grid_20261021); the baseline grid is not replaced'

engine_note: The child run uses --engine fast, the array twin of both the signal generator and the backtest engine. The twins are proved equivalent to the research path: results/signal_equivalence_check.json (268 symbols, 1 360 cells, no mismatch) and results/20261021_130000_grid_repro_fast (200 of 200 sampled baseline cells re-run through the fast path reproduce their stored summaries exactly).

measures_to_report.primary: pooled out-of-fold net PF of the selection procedure, computed with the walk-forward protocol of the survivor selection audit (results/20261021_121629_survivor_selection_audit, leg 3): the full sample of every symbol is cut into 5 sequential folds, at step k the best cell is chosen on the history (folds 1..k, at least 20 trades) and scored on fold k+1, which the selection never saw. The yardstick is the parent's pooled out-of-fold net PF of 0.6409 (0.4521 under 2x costs).
secondary: pooled full-sample net PF, gross net PF and trade count of the child against the parent
share of out-of-fold windows with net PF above 1, and above 1 under 2x costs
the OOS gate of the grid-wide audit (out-of-sample net PF > 1, at least 30 out-of-sample trades, still > 1 under 2x costs): how many cells of the child clear it, against 10 of 17 556 for the parent
the cost share of the gross P&L, recomputed on the child

decision_rule_fixed_in_advance: The child is promoted to a credible candidate only if (a) its pooled out-of-fold net PF under the identical walk-forward protocol is above 1.0, (b) it is still above 1.0 under 2x costs, and (c) at least one cell clears the OOS + 2x-cost gate with at least 30 out-of-sample trades. If any of the three fails, the child is recorded as a rejected mutation, whatever its in-sample numbers look like. A child that only improves the gross-to-net gap without crossing those gates is a cost-drag repair, not an edge.
guardrails: The child run writes to its own run directory and does not replace or modify the baseline grid.
No gate is relaxed to accommodate the child.
The result is recorded as parent -> child -> delta, and a negative result does not stop the program.
